title: China and Egypt Launch 'Eagles of Civilization 2026' Joint Air Drill — First-Ever J-16 vs. Rafale Combat Training
detail: Egyptian and Chinese air forces opened the flying phase of the 'Eagles of Civilization 2026' exercise on August 23, 2026, with People's Liberation Army Air Force J-16 fighters flying mock air-to-air combat against Egyptian Rafale and MiG-29M2 jets — the first-ever training encounter between the Chinese J-16 and the French-built Rafale, and the first deployment of Chinese J-16s to Africa. Six or more J-16s, escorted by a YY-20A aerial tanker plus KJ-500 airborne early warning, Y-20 transport, and Y-9 electronic-warfare aircraft, flew roughly 6,000 kilometers from western China to Egypt in about nine hours, landing at an Egyptian air base on August 21. It is the second joint China-Egypt air exercise, following an April 2025 round that paired lighter Chengdu J-10C fighters with Egyptian jets, and follows Egypt's China-observed 'Badr 2026' Sinai exercise in April as part of Cairo's deliberate military diversification away from exclusive US dependency. The drill, which includes air-superiority and search-and-rescue mission sets, is slated to run into early September 2026.

media.caption: A Chinese YY-20A tanker refuels J-16 fighters en route to Egypt for the 'Eagles of Civilization 2026' exercise
